description: kubectl and Helm: deletions, changes to a cluster, secret reads, shells in a container, and read commands.

rules.note: Deletion of resources, a Helm release, or the pods of a node. `-n` is the namespace, not a dry run.
The command changes objects in the cluster or runs a command in a pod.
`rollout restart`, `undo`, `pause`, and `resume` change a workload. `rollout status` and `history` only read.
`kubectl cp` reads or writes files in a container.

`get secret` with an output format (`-o yaml`, `-o json`, `-o jsonpath`, `-o go-template`) or with `--template` prints the secret data. A list of kinds (`get secrets,configmaps -o yaml`) does too. `-o name` and `-o wide` print names and sizes, and `describe secret` shows only sizes, so they are not here (dev round 4: kind lists, `--template`, names and sizes).

`kubectl -v=8` and higher prints the bodies of the API requests and responses, for example the data of a Secret that `describe secret` reads. Level 7 prints the request headers; kubectl masks the bearer token in them. kubectl has no `-vvv`: `-v` takes a number (dev round 4).
`config view --raw` and `--flatten` print client keys and tokens. `create token` prints a new token.
`helm get values` and `helm get all` print the release values, which often hold passwords. `manifest` and `hooks` print the rendered objects, Secrets included (`hooks` in dev round 4).

`helm status -o json` or `-o yaml` prints the whole release object, with the user-supplied values (`config`) and the manifest. `--debug` makes `install`, `upgrade`, and `status` print the user-supplied and computed values and the manifest. `helm list` and `helm history` print summaries only (dev round 4).

exemptions.note: `kubectl get secrets` lists names and `describe secret` shows sizes, also in a list of kinds (`get secrets,configmaps`, dev round 4). The rule `secret-values` flags the output options that print the data.
`--kubeconfig ~/.kube/config` uses the file to reach the cluster. It does not print or copy it.

safe.note: Reads of objects, logs, and cluster information.
Rollout state, access checks, and the current configuration without keys.
Local chart checks and release reads without values.
